title: Ultrahigh strength-ductility synergy in laser welded high carbon steel via quenching & partitioning treatment
abstract: This study investigates the effects of quenching & partitioning (Q&P) process on laser welded high-carbon steel (HCS) joint. The Q&P process achieved a multiphase microstructure consisting of martensite, retained austenite, and carbides in the welded joint. Remarkably, the treated joint exhibited superior mechanical properties, with an ultimate tensile strength of 1625 MPa and elongation of 21.4 %, fracturing in the base material (BM) during tensile testing. The enhanced performance is attributed to carbon enriched retained austenite, which activated the transformation induced plasticity (TRIP) effects, alongside precipitation strengthening from carbides. These results demonstrate that Q&P post weld treatment effectively optimizes microstructure and enhances mechanical performance, offering a rapid and industrially viable strategy for improving weld integrity in high-carbon steels.
